scenes.tts: Earth's oceans once rained rust. One reason is in your lungs right now.
scenes.visual: Vertical frame, no title. Full-height dark TEAL-tinted water from y -3.0 to 3.2. From the first frame RED flakes (small rough diamonds) are already falling slowly through the whole column, dozens of them, and landing on a thin red stripe at the bottom (y -3.0). The sea surface shimmers at y 3.2. No on-screen text calls it rain. On 'in your lungs': the view tilts up to the dark sky above the surface (y 3.2 to 5.4), where a few BLUE oxygen pips drift, and a horizontal GAUGE bar at the top draws on: 'O2 in air' (size 34), with a tick 'today' at its right end and the tag 'schematic'. The flakes never stop falling in this scene.
scenes.narration: Earth's oceans once rained rust. One reason is in your lungs right now.

scenes.tts: Rewind about three billion years. The air held almost no oxygen. And the sea held dissolved iron.
scenes.caption: Rewind about 3 billion years. The air held almost no oxygen. And the sea held dissolved iron.
scenes.visual: Do not throw the hook picture away: run it backward. On 'Rewind': the flakes stop, then rise back up the column, and as they rise each RED flake loosens into GREY discs, each with one small YELLOW dot on its rim; the falling thins to almost none and the red stripe at the bottom sinks to a faint trace: we have gone back before most of the rust. A readout under the gauge bar runs back and settles at 'about 3 billion years ago'. On 'almost no oxygen': the gauge bar drains to a thin sliver at its left end and the sky empties of pips. On 'dissolved iron': about 30 grey discs are now drifting through the whole column, each on its own slow path; the label 'dissolved iron' (size 34) lands after they settle.
scenes.narration: Rewind about 3 billion years. The air held almost no oxygen. And the sea held dissolved iron.

scenes.tts: At some point, tiny cells called cyanobacteria learned to pull electrons out of water, using sunlight. Their waste was oxygen.
scenes.visual: A rock ledge juts from the left wall at y 2.0, just under the surface. One GREEN capsule cell with a notch (mouth) settles on it on 'tiny cells', large enough to read (about 2.5 units long); it is seen before it is named, and the label 'cyanobacteria' (size 34) lands on that word. On 'pull electrons': two TEAL droplets, each holding two yellow dots, enter the mouth. On 'using sunlight': a GOLD ray from a sun at top right strikes the capsule and the four yellow dots are pulled inside and kept. On 'Their waste': one BLUE bubble pops out of the capsule's vent and rises. The capsule multiplies along the ledge into a GREEN mat and the bubbles become a steady stream.
scenes.narration: At some point, tiny cells called cyanobacteria learned to pull electrons out of water, using sunlight. Their waste was oxygen.

scenes.tts: But the air did not fill with it right away. Oxygen strongly pulls in electrons, and that iron had electrons to give. So the iron handed them over, turned into a kind of rust, and sank.
scenes.visual: On 'did not fill': the bubbles rise from the mat but fade before the surface; the gauge sliver at the top does not move, and it pulses to show it has not. On 'strongly pulls in': the view pushes in on ONE bubble in mid-column until it is 2.5 units across: a BLUE disc with four empty dashed sockets on its rim. On 'electrons to give': four GREY iron discs close in, yellow dots first. On 'handed them over': the four yellow dots jump into the four sockets one after another; each iron disc turns RED as its dot leaves. On 'kind of rust': the four red discs clump into one RED flake and the blue bubble is gone; the tag 'rust-like mineral' (size 34) sits on the flake for a beat. On 'and sank': the flake drops; pull back to the full column, where it is happening everywhere and red flakes fall the whole height of the frame, the hook picture again, now explained.
scenes.narration: But the air did not fill with it right away. Oxygen strongly pulls in electrons, and that iron had electrons to give. So the iron handed them over, turned into a kind of rust, and sank.

scenes.tts: That rust helped build stripes of rock. We still mine them for iron.
scenes.visual: The view rides a flake down to the sea floor. On 'helped build': flakes land as a RED stripe at y -3.0; a pale GREY stripe grows on it; red; grey: seven stripes stack upward to about y -1.4 in three seconds. The label 'banded iron formation' (size 34) lands once the stack is visible; the name is on screen only, not spoken. On 'still mine them': a white bracket closes on the stack and a plain pick-and-block icon in TEXT white taps it. No other tag. The view starts back up the column before the scene ends.
scenes.narration: That rust helped build stripes of rock. We still mine them for iron.

scenes.tts: Volcanic gases, methane, and rock on land took oxygen too. Then, between about two point four and two point one billion years ago, oxygen rose, wavered, and stayed. It was still far below today's level.
scenes.caption: Volcanic gases, methane, and rock on land took oxygen too. Then, between about 2.4 and 2.1 billion years ago, oxygen rose, wavered, and stayed. It was still far below today's level.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full column and tilt up so the sky and the gauge bar are in frame. A few bubbles now break the surface as blue pips. On 'Volcanic gases': a GREY puff with a yellow dot drifts in from the left edge and takes one pip (dot jumps, pip gone). On 'methane': a grey ring rising from the sea floor takes another. On 'rock on land': a grey rock block on a wedge of shore at upper left takes a third and goes dull (only iron turns red). On 'between about': the readout changes to 'about 2.4 to 2.1 billion years ago' (the numbers are on screen as they are said). On 'oxygen rose': pips that break the surface now stay and the gauge bar climbs. On 'wavered': the bar drops back and climbs again, and the pips wink out and return. On 'and stayed': the bar settles at a low steady level and four or five pips drift in the sky; tag 'schematic; levels uncertain'. On 'far below': a white double-headed arrow opens along the bar between the low level and the 'today' tick. Draw no cause for the rise. The rust keeps falling below and the stack keeps its stripes.
scenes.narration: Volcanic gases, methane, and rock on land took oxygen too. Then, between about 2.4 and 2.1 billion years ago, oxygen rose, wavered, and stayed. It was still far below today's level.

scenes.tts: The air only keeps the oxygen that nothing else takes first. So your next breath? Leftovers.
scenes.visual: The full column, everything running at once: mat streaming, grey takers taking, flakes falling onto the striped stack, four or five pips above. On 'only keeps': one bubble is traced by a thin blue line from the mat's vent, past the iron, through the surface, into the sky; a second bubble on the same path is taken by an iron disc half-way up. On 'your next breath': the readout changes to 'today'; the grey iron discs fade out and the flakes stop falling; the striped stack stays; the gauge bar cross-fades (no sweep) to full at the 'today' tick and the sky fills with drifting BLUE pips. On 'Leftovers': the pips drift toward the viewer and swell, while far below the red striped stack still sits on the sea floor.
scenes.narration: The air only keeps the oxygen that nothing else takes first. So your next breath? Leftovers.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed, still-moving column as it stands at 'today' (no iron discs, no falling flakes; the striped stack on the floor; pips drifting), centred near y +1.2: 'Every breath is oxygen that nothing else took first.' Beneath it: 'Free at biochemistrypedia.com'. Nothing in y -4.6 to -3.2.
